Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:10:1.hebrew: איכא בינייהו נחש - דת"ק חשיב ליה בהדי הנך ובעי כ"ג, ור"ע באינך סבירא ליה כוותיה, בר מנחש, כדאמרינן בארבעה אבות נזיקין (שם דף טו:): נחש מועד לעולם, דברי הכל:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:10:1.english: The difference between them is a snake - For the first tanna counts it together with those [animals] and requires twenty-three [judges], and Rabbi Akiva agrees with him regarding the others, except for a snake, as we say in [the chapter] Arba’ah Avot Nezikin (ibid., daf 15b): "A snake is always an attested danger, according to everyone."

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:11:1.hebrew: לענין ע"ז - חלק בין יחידים למרובים, דעיר הנדחת בעי סנהדרי גדולה, כדיליף לקמן (סנהדרין דף טז.), ויחיד נידון בכ"ג, דכתיב (דברים י״ז:ה׳): "והוצאת את האיש ההוא וגו' אל שעריך" — ב"ד שבשעריך:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:11:1.english: With regard to idol worship - [The Torah] distinguished between individuals and multitudes, for an idolatrous city requires the Great Sanhedrin, as [the Gemara] derives below (Sanhedrin 16a), whereas an individual is judged by twenty-three [judges], as it is written (Deuteronomy 17:5): "And you shall bring forth that man... unto your gates" — [meaning,] the court that is in your gates.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:12:1.hebrew: למימרא - דשבט שלם שהודח, בדינא דרבים דיינינן ליה — כדינא דעיר הנדחת, דמיקרי מרובין — דיינינן ליה בסייף ובסנהדרי גדולה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:12:1.english: Is this to say - That an entire tribe that was led astray, we judge it under the law of a multitude — like the law of an idolatrous city, which is called "many" — [namely,] we judge it with the sword and by the Great Sanhedrin:

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:12:2.hebrew: מעשרה ועד מאה - בציר מעשרה לא מקרי עיר, וטפי ממאה נפקא מתורת עיר והוו להו ציבור, ובציבור לא כתיב סייף. הלכך, כל א' נידון בפני עצמו ובסקילה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:12:2.english: From ten until one hundred - Less than ten is not called a city; and more than one hundred departs from the category of a city, and they become a community, and regarding a community [execution by] the sword is not written. Therefore, each one is judged on his own, and by stoning.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:1:1.hebrew: אימא לקטלא - לחייב מיתה לבעליו, וניחייביה מיתה, והיכי מפקינן לה מפשטיה לגמרי:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:1:1.english: Say [that it comes] for execution - To make its owner liable to the death penalty, and let us hold him liable to the death penalty; and how can we remove [the verse] entirely from its plain meaning?

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:2:1.hebrew: אי כתב הכי - קושיא היא, כלומר: איצטריך יומת לדונו במיתה האמורה בתורה סתם — דאינו אלא חנק — דלא תימא: גם בעליו יסקל:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:2:1.english: Had [the Merciful One] written this - This is an objection. That is to say: [The word] "shall be put to death" was necessary [in order] to sentence him to the death [penalty] stated in the Torah without specification — which is none other than strangulation — so that you should not say: "Its owner also" shall be stoned.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:2:2.hebrew: קטל איהו בסייף - דקי"ל לקמן (סנהדרין ד' נב), רוצח בסייף:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:2:2.english: [If] he killed [the person] himself, [he is executed] by the sword - For we maintain later on (Sanhedrin 52b) [that] a murderer [is executed] by the sword:

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:2:3.hebrew: קטל שורו נימא בסקילה - דחמירה מכולן? בתמיה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:2:3.english: [If] his ox killed, shall we say [he is executed] by stoning - Which is the most severe of all [forms of execution]?! [This is said] in astonishment.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:3:1.hebrew: הניחא - הא דעקרת ליה לקרא מפשטיה, ולא מוקמינן ליה למיתת חנק ממש:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:3:1.english: This works out well - This [fact] that you uprooted the verse from its plain meaning, and we do not establish it as [referring to] actual death by strangulation:

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:3:2.hebrew: למ"ד חנק חמור - מסייף, בפ' ד' מיתות (לקמן סנהדרין נ:). הלכך, איכא למיפרך: קטל איהו בסייף, קטל שורו בחנק:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:3:2.english: According to the one who says [that] strangulation is [more] severe - Than the sword, in the chapter [entitled] Arba Mitot (below, Sanhedrin 50b). Therefore, there is [room] to refute [this]: [If] he himself killed, [he is executed] by the sword; [yet if] his ox killed, [shall he be executed] by strangulation?!

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:3:3.hebrew: אלא למ"ד חנק קל - אימא: למיתת חנק אתא:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:3:3.english: But according to the one who says strangulation is lighter - Say that it comes for the death penalty of strangulation.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:5:1.hebrew: משום היא גופה - משום הך קשיא גופא: דלא תימא "לא תקחו כופר" כתב רחמנא וליקטול — כתב רחמנא "ונתן פדיון נפשו", למימר דהיכא דקטל איהו לא תסגי ליה בממונא כו', אבל קטל שורו — סגי ליה בממונא, ואי לא יהיב כופר — חייב חנק:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:5:1.english: Because of this itself - Because of this very difficulty: so that you should not say, "The Merciful One wrote 'You shall not take a ransom' — and let him be executed"; [rather,] the Merciful One wrote "and he shall give the redemption of his life," to say that where he [himself] killed, money does not suffice for him, etc., but [where] his ox killed, money suffices for him; and if he does not give a ransom, he is liable to strangulation.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:6:1.hebrew: שור סיני - בהמה שקרבה להר בעוד שהשכינה שם, דכתיב: "אם בהמה אם איש לא יחיה":
Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:6:1.english: An ox [at Mount] Sinai - An animal that approached the mountain while the Divine Presence was there, as it is written: “Whether animal or man, it shall not live” (Exodus 19:13).

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:6:2.english: By how many - [By how many] judges is it judged?

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:6:3.hebrew: מה איש בכ"ג - דאיש פשיטא לן, דכבר הוקבעו לישראל סנהדראות מיתרו ואילך:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:6:3.english: Just as a person [is judged] by twenty-three - For [regarding] a person, it is obvious to us, as Sanhedrins had already been established for Israel from [the time of] Jethro onward.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:7:1.hebrew: ברדלס - חיה היא, ובלע"ז קורין אות' פוטויו"ש:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:7:1.english: Bardelas - It is a wild animal, and in Old French they call it putois [polecat].

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:7:2.hebrew: אמר ריש לקיש - הא דאמר ר' אליעזר, "כל הקודם להורגן זכה" — והוא שהמיתו נפש; ואמילתא דת"ק, דאיירי כשהמיתו, קאי ר' אליעזר:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:7:2.english: Reish Lakish says - That which Rabbi Eliezer said, "Whoever is first to kill them has acquired [benefit]," is [specifically] where they killed a person; and Rabbi Eliezer is addressing the statement of the first Tanna, who is dealing with [a case where] they killed [a person].

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:7:3.hebrew: יש להם תרבות - מותר לגדלן, לפי שאדם יכול ללמדן שלא יזיקו. הלכך, שם בעלים נקרא עליהן ולא הוי כהפקר, ואסור להורגן אם לא המיתו. אבל אם המיתו, סופן מוכיח על תחילתן שלא אלו בני תרבות, ואין צריכין לדונן:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:7:3.english: They have [the capacity for] domestication - It is permitted to raise them, because a person can train them not to cause damage. Therefore, the status of ownership applies to them, and they are not like ownerless property, and it is forbidden to kill them if they have not killed. But if they have killed, their end proves their beginning, that these are not tame creatures, and there is no need to judge them.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:7:4.hebrew: ר' יוחנן אמר אע"ג שלא המיתו - א"ר אליעזר: "כל הקודם להרגן זכה". וה"ק ליה לת"ק: דקאמרת כשהמיתו צריכי כ"ג דיינין — אני אומר אפילו לא המיתו מותר להורגן כל הקודם, וכ"ש אם המיתו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:7:4.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says: Even though they did not kill - Rabbi Eliezer said: "Whoever is first to kill them acquires merit." And this is what he was saying to the first Tanna: "[As for that] which you say, that when they killed they require twenty-three judges — I say [that] even if they did not kill, it is permitted for anyone who is first to kill them, and all the more so if they killed."

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:7:5.hebrew: ואין להם בעלים - כלומר, אין שם הבעלים חל עליהם, ולא הוו אלא כהפקר, לפי שלא היה לו לגדלן:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:7:5.english: And they do not have owners - That is to say, the status of ownership does not apply to them, and they are nothing other than ownerless, since he should not have raised them.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:8:1.english: He won - Implies that he profited.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:8:2.hebrew: זכה בעורן - העור שלו, כיון דאין להם בעלים:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:8:2.english: [He] merits their hide - The hide is his, since they have no owner.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:8:3.hebrew: כיון דהמיתו - ואמור רבנן דאין צריך לדונן בב"ד, הוו להו כמאן דגמר דינייהו, ואסירי בהנאה — כדקי"ל: "שאם שחטו לאחר שנגמר דינו — אסור", בפרק שור שנגח (ב"ק מא.):
Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:8:3.english: Since they killed - And the Sages said that there is no need to judge them in court, so they are considered like those whose verdict has been finalized, and they are forbidden for benefit — as we maintain: "If one slaughtered it after its verdict was finalized, it is forbidden," in the chapter entitled Shor SheNagach (Bava Kamma 41a):

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15b:9:1.english: He acquired [it] for Heaven - He performed a righteous deed:

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 15b:12:1.hebrew: מעשרה עד ק' - הא דלמר חשיב עיר בק' ולמר בעשרה, נראה דפליגי בקרא דעמוס ה', דכתיב: "העיר היוצאת אלף תשאיר מאה, והיוצאת מאה תשאיר עשרה":
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 15b:12:1.english: "From ten until one hundred" - As for that which according to one Master [it] is considered a city with one hundred [people], and according to the [other] Master with ten [people] — it appears that they disagree regarding the verse in Amos 5, as it is written: "The city that went out a thousand shall have a hundred left, and that which went out a hundred shall have ten left."

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 15b:1:1.hebrew: אימא לקטלא הוא דאתא - תימה, דמשמע דאי לקטלא אתא — תו לא דרשינן מיניה "כמיתת בעלים כך מיתת השור". ותימה: הא גבי רובע, דדריש לעיל מדאיתקיש! וכ"ת משום דחדא מיתה כתיב אתרווייהו, דכתיב "והרגת את האשה ואת הבהמה" — הא גבי שוכב דרשינן מדאיתקיש, אע"ג דכתיב מיתה בכל חד באפי נפשיה: "ואיש כי יתן שכבתו בבהמה מות יומת" וגו'! וי"ל דהתם בהמה כתיב בתריה, לאקשויי בהמה לאיש; אבל הכא כתיב שור ברישא והדר בעלים, לאקשויי בעלים לשור, ולא שור לבעלים — אי לאו משום דמייתר, דלא איצטריך לגופיה. וא"ת: והא אכתי אצטריך "יומת" למיתה בידי שמים, כדדרשינן באלו נערות (כתובות לז: ושם): לפי שמצינו מומתין בידי שמים נותנין ממון ומתכפר להם, שנאמר "ואם כופר יושת עליו"? וי"ל דאי למיתה בידי שמים לחוד אתא, הל"ל "ימות", אבל "יומת" משמע בב"ד; לכך מוקמי ליה למיתה ממש, או לכמיתת בעלים כך מיתת השור. ומ"מ כי מוקמינן ליה לכמיתת בעלים כו', דרשינן נמי מיתה בידי שמים, דאין מקרא יוצא מידי פשוטו, דמשמע דבעלים חייבין מיתה. ועי"ל דה"פ: ואימא לקטלא נמי הוא דאתא, ולא למעוטי דרשה דכמיתת בעלים כך מיתת השור קא אתי, דקדרשינן ליה נמי מדאיתקש:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 15b:1:1.english: "Say that it comes for execution" - This is astonishing, for it implies that if it came for execution, we would no longer derive from it: "Just as the death of the owner, so is the death of the ox." And this is astonishing: for regarding [an animal that] copulated [with a woman, rova], [the Gemara] derived [the court size] above from the fact that they were juxtaposed! And if you say [that this is] because a single [mention of] death is written regarding both of them, as it is written: "And you shall kill the woman and the beast" (Leviticus 20:16) — behold, regarding one who lies [with an animal, shokhev], we derive [it] from the fact that they were juxtaposed, even though death is written for each one on its own: "And if a man lies with a beast, he shall surely be put to death" etc. (ibid. 20:15)! And one can say that there, the beast is written after him, to compare the beast to the man; but here, the ox is written first and then the owner, to compare the owner to the ox, and not the ox to the owner — were it not for the fact that it is superfluous, in that it was not needed for itself. And if you say: But is not "shall be put to death" still needed for death at the hands of Heaven, as we derive in [the chapter entitled] Elu Na'arot (Ketubot 37b and elsewhere): "Since we find that those liable to death at the hands of Heaven pay money and achieve atonement, as it is stated: 'If ransom be laid upon him'" (Exodus 21:30)? And one can say that if it came solely for death at the hands of Heaven, it should have said "he shall die" [yamut], whereas "shall be put to death" [yumat] implies [execution] by a court; therefore, we establish it [as referring] to actual execution, or to [the principle that] "just as the death of the owner, so is the death of the ox." And nevertheless, when we establish it for "just as the death of the owner, etc.," we also derive death at the hands of Heaven, as a verse does not depart from its plain meaning, which implies that the owner is liable to death. And furthermore one can say that this is the explanation: "And say that it comes for execution as well" — and it did not come to exclude the derivation that "just as the death of the owner, so is the death of the ox," for we would derive that as well from the fact that they were juxtaposed.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 15b:6:1.hebrew: שור סיני בכמה - איש סיני לא קמיבעיא ליה, כדמוכח בסמוך, דדריש: "אם בהמה אם איש — מה איש בכ"ג", משמע דאיש פשיטא ליה; אע"ג דאכתי לא מכתב קרא ד"ושפטו העדה והצילו העדה" (במדבר ל״ה:כ״ה), מ"מ כיון דתקון יתרו סנהדראות, סתמא דמילתא סנהדרי קטנה נמי לדיני נפשות תקון. וא"ת: ומאי קמיבעיא ליה משור סיני, דמ"נ מינה? מאי דהוה הוה! וכן קשה בפ"ב דמסכת ע"ז (דף לד.): "במה שימש משה כל ז' ימי המילואים?". ושמא מיבעי ליה למיסבר קראי, כדאשכחן פ"ק דיומא (ד' ה. ושם) גבי כיצד הלבישן:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 15b:6:1.english: An ox at Sinai, by how many - [The dilemma] was not raised concerning a person at Sinai, as is proven nearby [in the Gemara], where it expounds: "Whether animal or man" — just as a man is [judged] by twenty-three, which implies that [the law regarding] a man was obvious to him. Even though the verse "And the congregation shall judge... and the congregation shall deliver" (Numbers 35:25) had not yet been written, nevertheless, since Jethro established Sanhedrins, the presumption is that they also established a Small Sanhedrin for capital cases. And if you say: But what dilemma did he have regarding an ox at Sinai? What difference does it make — what was, was! And similarly, a difficulty arises in the second chapter of Tractate Avodah Zarah (34a): In what did Moses minister all seven days of the inauguration? And perhaps he needed [to resolve this] in order to understand the verses, as we find in the first chapter of Yoma (5a and there) regarding: "How did he dress them?".

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 15b:6:2.hebrew: מי גמרי' שעה מדורות או לא - תימה: הא אפילו דורות מדורות לא ילפינן לעיל, דמיבעי לן קרא לרובע ונרבע ושור הנסקל! וי"ל, דהכא אית לן למילף טפי, משום דכל דיני סקילה ילפינן לקמן מסיני בפרק נגמר הדין (סנהדרין דף מה.): מניין שבדחייה הוא? ת"ל "ירה"; מניין שבסקילה? ת"ל "סקול":
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 15b:6:2.english: Do we derive [a law for a specific] time from [laws for all] generations, or not? - [This is] puzzling: For even [one case applying to all] generations from [another case applying to all] generations we do not derive earlier, as we require a verse for [an animal that] copulates [with a human] and [an animal that is] copulated with, and [for] an ox that is to be stoned! And one can say that here we have [reason] to derive [it] all the more, because all laws of stoning we derive later from Sinai, in the chapter [entitled] Nigmar HaDin (Sanhedrin 45a): "From where [is it derived] that it is by pushing down? The verse states: 'He shall be shot' [Exodus 19:13]. From where [is it derived] that it is by stoning? The verse states: 'He shall be stoned' [ibid.]."

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 15b:7:1.hebrew: והברדלס - פ"ה: פוטיי"ש. ולא משמע כן, דאותו אינו עז כל כך, וכאן משמע שהוא עז ביותר ודרכו להמית את האדם. וכן בפרק אלו מציאות (ב"מ דף כד.) אמרי': "המציל מן הארי ומן הדוב כו'"; ובפ"ק דב"ק (טו: ושם) תנן: "הרי אלו מועדים". ואפשר שהוא מין נחש, דהא מפרש התם בגמ' (טז: ושם) דברדלס היינו אפא, וצבוע זהו אפא, וצבוע זהו אפעה — שהרי "גיא הצבועים" מתרגמינן "מישר אפעיא" (שמואל א יג), וכתיב "אפעה ושרף מעופף" (ישעיהו ל׳:ו׳). ומיהו יש עדיין ברדלס אחר, דהא בפ"ק דבכורות (דף ח.) חשיב אפעה לע' שנה, ברדלס לג' שנים; ואע"ג דחשיב לה התם בהדי זאב וארי, ע"כ לאו היינו ההוא דהכא ודב"ק, דהא מפרש התם דהיינו אפא דהוא אפעה. ויתכן דההוא דבכורות הוא פוטיי"ש שפ"ה בכאן. וכן ההיא דפ"ק דפסחים (דף ט.) "אם חולדה וברדלס מצויין שם" — משמע שהיא חיה קטנה כעין חולדה:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 15b:7:1.english: "And the bardelas" - Rashi explained: putois [polecat]. But this does not seem [correct], for that [animal] is not so ferocious, whereas here it implies that it is exceedingly ferocious and its manner is to kill a human. And similarly, in the chapter [entitled] Elu Metzi'ot (Bava Metzia 24a), we say: "One who rescues [property] from a lion, and from a bear, etc."; and in the first chapter of Bava Kamma (15b, and there), we learned [in a mishna]: "These are forewarned." And it is possible that it is a type of snake, for behold, there in the Gemara (16b, and there) [the Gemara] explains that a bardelas is an apa, and a tzavua is an apa, and a tzavua is an ef'eh [viper] — as we translate "the valley of Tzavo'im" [into Aramaic] as "the plain of vipers [meishar af'aya]" (I Samuel 13), and it is written: "Viper [ef'eh] and flying serpent" (Isaiah 30:6). However, there is still another [creature called] bardelas, for behold, in the first chapter of Bekhorot (8a), [the Gemara] reckons [the gestation period of] a viper as seventy years, [and that of] a bardelas as three years; and even though it reckons it there alongside a wolf and a lion, perforce that is not the same one as here and in Bava Kamma, for there it explains that it is an apa, which is an ef'eh. And it is likely that the one in Bekhorot is the putois that Rashi explained here. And similarly, that [statement] in the first chapter of Pesachim (9a): "If a weasel and a bardelas are commonly found there" — this implies that it is a small animal, similar to a weasel.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 15b:7:2.hebrew: ור' יוחנן אמר אע"פ שלא המיתו - אדר"א דמתני' קאי, דקסבר: (אית) להם תרבות ואין להם בעלים. ותימה, דבפ"ק דב"ק (דף טו:) תנן: "ר"א אומר: בזמן שהם בני תרבות — אינן מועדים"! ואומר ר"ת, דהתם גרס: "ר' אלעזר", שמזכירו אחר ר"מ התם בגמרא; והכא ר' אליעזר, שהוא קודם ר"ע. ומיהו, אכתי קשה: דהתם תנן: "והנחש מועד לעולם", אליבא דכ"ע; והכא קאמר ריש לקיש: "והוא שהמיתו, אבל לא המיתו לא, דיש להם תרבות ויש להם בעלים" — אפי' נחש! ושמא יש לחלק: דלענין דאין להורגן כל הקודם קאמר הכא דיש להם תרבות, אפי' נחש, אבל לא לענין נזק שלם. ועוד אר"ת: תרבות דהתם — הוא שגידלם בביתו; ותרבות דהכא — היינו בקשורים בשלשלאות, כגון ארי בגוהרקי שלו, דאין להורגם אלא כשהמיתו, אפי' נחש:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 15b:7:2.english: "And Rabbi Yoḥanan says: Even though they did not kill" - This refers to the statement of Rabbi Eliezer of our Mishnah, as he holds that they have or: do not have the capacity for domestication and they have no owners. And this is puzzling, for in the first chapter of Bava Kamma (15b) we learned in a mishna: Rabbi Eliezer says: When they are domesticated, they are not forewarned! And Rabbeinu Tam says that there the reading is Rabbi Elazar, as the Gemara mentions him there after Rabbi Meir in the Gemara; whereas here it is Rabbi Eliezer, who preceded Rabbi Akiva. However, it is still difficult: for there we learned in a mishna: "And the snake is always forewarned," according to everyone; yet here Reish Lakish says: "And that is specifically when they killed; but if they did not kill, no, as they have the capacity for domestication and they have owners" — even a snake! And perhaps one can distinguish: that regarding that anyone who comes first may not kill them, the Gemara states here that they have the capacity for domestication, even a snake; but not regarding full damage. And furthermore Rabbeinu Tam said: The domestication of that case is where one raised them in his house; but the domestication of here means when they are tied with chains, such as a lion in its cage, where one may not kill them unless they killed, even a snake.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 15b:8:1.hebrew: מאי זכה זכה לעורן - במרובה (ב"ק דף פ: ושם), גבי חתול — כולהו מודו דזכה לעורו:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 15b:8:1.english: What does he merit? He merits their hides - In [the chapter entitled] Merubah (Bava Kamma 80b, and see there), regarding a cat, everyone agrees that he merits its hide.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 15b:9:1.hebrew: תניא כוותיה דר"ל - הא דלא חשיב הך בריש החולץ (יבמות דף לו. ושם) בהדי תלת דהלכה כר"ל — משום דהכא אליבא דר"א פליגי:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 15b:9:1.english: "It is taught in accordance with Reish Lakish" - The fact that [the Gemara] does not count this [case] at the beginning of [the chapter entitled] HaCholetz (Yevamot 36a, and there) among the three [cases] where the halakha is in accordance with Reish Lakish is because here they disagree according to [the opinion of] Rabbi Eliezer.
